title: live-ui-test and relay-test paired through the legacy ?pin= query, not the QR's #pin=
body:
## Summary
The device harnesses never exercised the fragment path every real phone takes.

## Description
core PairingUrl.of puts the PIN in the fragment so a relay cannot log it; the page keeps ?pin= as a fallback. tools/live-ui-test.mjs:52 and tools/relay-test.mjs:175, :226 paired with ?pin=, so the QR path never ran against a real TV or relay, and over the relay the harness put the PIN back in the request line. Fixed to #pin=; device-rules-test pins it.

## Flow
- live-ui-test opens BASE/?pin=NNNN
- the TV QR says BASE/#pin=NNNN
- the shipped path is untested on device

## Expected impact
The device run proves the pairing a viewer actually does. Could break: nothing on the page (companion-refusal-test proves both forms pair).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - harness drives the shipped path
Before: 0/3 harness pairings via the fragment
After: 3/3
Method: gate - device-rules-test source pin, red then green; node --check
Result: better
Gate: none

title: pen-sim, latency-probe and tail-diag exit 1 (FAIL) when the TV refuses the PIN
body:
## Summary
A run that never started reported the same code as a measured failure.

## Description
The harness codes are 0 pass, 1 FAIL, 2 could not run (pairingPin, socket error), 3 crash. A refused hello exited 1 in tools/pen-sim.mjs:32, tools/latency-probe.mjs:37, tools/tail-diag.mjs:87, so a stale --pin read as an ink or latency regression. Registry: error-handling exit-contract-is-a-taxonomy-projection. Now exit 2, message unchanged.

## Flow
- run latency-probe with a stale --pin
- TV answers welcome{accepted:false}
- exit 1, indistinguishable from "p95 over 25 ms"

## Expected impact
A script or person reading exit codes can tell setup from regression. Could break: a caller that branched on 1 for refusal (none in the tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - exit code names the failure kind
Before: 0/3 tools exit "could not run" on refusal
After: 3/3 (each of two seeded back to 1 goes red)
Method: gate - device-rules-test with a loopback fake TV, red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/pen-sim.mjs:31-32, tools/latency-probe.mjs:36-37, tools/tail-diag.mjs:86-87 `pairing rejected` -> process.exit(1); live-ui-test.mjs:352 exit 3; device.mjs pairingPin exit 2

title: device.mjs runs adb from one hard-coded operator path, ignoring ANDROID_HOME
body:
## Summary
ADB_BIN was `process.env.ADB ??` the operator's scoop path (tools/device.mjs:26).

## Description
On any other machine every adb call (screencap, logcat PIN, keyevents, relay relaunch) was an ENOENT, and the machine's own ANDROID_HOME/ANDROID_SDK_ROOT was ignored. resolveAdb() now takes $ADB, the operator path where it exists (unchanged there), the SDK env vars, then adb on the PATH; pure and tested.

## Flow
- clone on a second machine with ANDROID_HOME set
- node tools/pen-sim.mjs with no --pin
- execFileSync ENOENT on the operator path

## Expected impact
The harness runs for anyone with an SDK. Could break: nothing on the operator machine (the path still wins where it exists).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - portability
Before: 0/3 non-operator cases resolve a runnable adb
After: 3/3 (ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, PATH)
Method: gate - device-rules-test "resolveAdb", red against HEAD then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: jsqr is a tools/ dependency no committed file imports
body:
## Summary
tools/package.json declared jsqr ^1.4.0 with zero consumers.

## Description
jsqr came in with 991f1a0d for a QR check an executor ran by hand (.cx stop S3); no gate was committed. Zero-consumer grep over tracked .mjs/.cjs/.js/.ts/.py/.ps1 and the main checkout's tools/ and uat/: no import. Removed from package.json and the lock; the lock is what npm writes (package-lock-only, offline, unchanged).

## Flow
- npm ci --prefix tools installs jsqr
- nothing loads it

## Expected impact
One fewer package in every tools/ install and supply-chain inventory. Could break: an ad-hoc QR check (re-add when one is committed).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - dependency surface
Before: 4 direct deps, 2 lock entries for jsqr
After: 3 direct deps, 0
Method: gate - npm install --package-lock-only --offline in a temp copy (exit 0, lock unchanged); device-rules-test and companion-refusal-test green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: git grep -n "jsqr|jsQR" -- ':!**/package-lock.json' -> tools/package.json:11 only; git show --stat 991f1a0d (no consumer)

title: Two phones on the relay stub evict each other about once a second, forever
body:
## Summary
relay-stub closes the previous pen with a bare close when a new one attaches (tools/relay-stub.mjs:81).

## Description
A bare close reads to the companion as a dropped line, so the evicted phone redials (backoff resets to 1 s on every welcome), attaches, and evicts the other, which does the same. On the LAN transport the TV tells the older pen "another pen took over" and it stands down. The stub "must stay dumb", so the fix is a choice: a close code the page treats as a takeover, or forward the TV's refusal before closing. relay-test 5b closes tab 1 before opening tab 2, so the loop never shows.

## Flow
- phone A pairs through the relay
- phone B opens the QR
- stub closes A; A redials and closes B; repeat

## Expected impact
A second viewer on the relay path does not fight the first. Could break: the "relay stays dumb" contract if the stub learns message meaning.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one takeover, then stable
Before: walked: unbounded alternation at ~1 s
After: not built
Method: simulation - code walk of attach() and the companion's onclose/backoff
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: tools/relay-stub.mjs:80-83 `pen?.close(); pen = ws;`; companion/index.html onclose -> scheduleReconnect(); onMessage welcome -> backoff = BACKOFF_MIN_MS
instrument: two companion tabs (Playwright) against tools/relay-stub.mjs with a ws client as the TV answering hellos: count pen attaches and hellos in 30 s (LAN behaviour: 1 takeover, then silence)

title: dev.ps1 hard-codes the operator's SDK and overwrites JAVA_HOME unconditionally
body:
## Summary
scripts/dev.ps1:45-47 set $sdk and $env:JAVA_HOME to fixed paths on the operator's machine.

## Description
device.mjs now resolves adb portably (9b501596); dev.ps1 still points adb, the emulator and gradle's JAVA_HOME at C:\Users\kazda paths, so the cycle cannot run on another machine and overrides a JAVA_HOME a developer set. Same fallback order as resolveAdb: keep the operator path where it exists, else ANDROID_HOME/ANDROID_SDK_ROOT and the caller's JAVA_HOME.

## Flow
- run ./scripts/dev.ps1 on a second machine
- adb.exe not found under the operator path

## Expected impact
The full cycle is runnable beyond one laptop. Could break: the operator's JAVA_HOME selection if the order is wrong (keep the JBR where it exists).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - portability
Before: 3 fixed paths, 0 env fallbacks
After: not built
Method: simulation - read dev.ps1
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: device-rules-test: cut a Resolve-Toolchain function out of dev.ps1 with the PowerShell parser (as Initialize-LiveTools is) and run it with stubbed env and Test-Path

title: latency-probe and tail-diag leave a 6-15 s random scribble committed on the TV
body:
## Summary
Their synthetic pen load ends with phase "up", which PenEngine commits as a stroke of thousands of random points.

## Description
tools/latency-probe.mjs:58-89 and tools/tail-diag.mjs:215-232 stream random points at 60 Hz then send up; PenEngine.handlePen commits any stroke of 2+ points, adding an undo entry and a full-frame scribble to the viewer's paused frame. An undo after the run would clean it while paused, but tail-diag --nopause would make that undo a seek trip (TransportPlan visit), so the fix needs a rule per mode.

## Flow
- run latency-probe on the Stick
- the paused frame now carries a scribble
- the next live-ui-test clears it with D-pad Down

## Expected impact
A probe leaves the TV as it found it. Could break: the --nopause measurement if the cleanup moves the player.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - probes are side-effect free
Before: walked: 1 committed annotation per run
After: not built
Method: simulation - code walk of the probes and PenEngine.handlePen
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: tools/latency-probe.mjs:89 `ws.send({type:"pen",phase:"up",...})`; core PenEngine.kt handlePen "up" -> commit(finished) when points >= 2
instrument: the loopback fake TV from device-rules-test running a core-like counter: annotations committed after `latency-probe --seconds 1` and `tail-diag --seconds 1` (want 0, or an undo sent when paused)

title: relay-test's round-trip probe ignores a refused hello and reports "no probes answered"
body:
## Summary
measureRelayRtt (tools/relay-test.mjs:66-104) listens only for pongs.

## Description
If the TV refuses the probe's hello (a PIN rotated by a relaunch, a lockout), every ping is dropped before pairing and the check says "relay round-trip measured: no probes answered", the same words as a dead relay. pen-sim and the probes print "pairing rejected: <reason>"; this one does not.

## Flow
- relay-test reaches section 6 after a TV relaunch
- hello refused
- FAIL "no probes answered", reason lost

## Expected impact
A relay-test failure names its cause. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - failure says why
Before: walked: refusal reported as no answers
After: not built
Method: simulation - read measureRelayRtt
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: tools/relay-test.mjs:83-89 on("message") handles only m.type === "pong"; :253 check("relay round-trip measured", false, "no probes answered")
instrument: export measureRelayRtt (or its message handler) and drive it against a loopback fake relay that refuses the hello: want a refusal reason in the check detail instead of "no probes answered"
